title: Morning Market Update
prompt: Use my installed market-update skill to deliver a single, readable US market snapshot PNG as the primary briefing, with a prominent factual headline and a clearly labeled one-sentence interpretation at the top of the image (roughly 30–40 words combined, at most 40). Use Massive first for market data. Cover: (1) SPY and QQQ regular-session closing prices and daily dollar/percentage changes; (2) 2-, 10-, and 30-year US Treasury yields and basis-point changes; (3) market breadth for a clearly named universe, or an explicitly labeled RSP-versus-SPY participation proxy, plus the strongest and weakest US sectors using all 11 sector ETF proxies, labeling incomplete coverage; (4) a compact snapshot of VIX, the US dollar, oil, and gold with levels and daily changes, naming benchmarks or ETF proxies accurately and adding commentary only for notable moves; (5) the previous day's major economic events and market-moving news, including Fed decisions, CPI, PMI, employment and other relevant releases, with actual versus consensus when verified; (6) the next US session's top 2–3 verified upcoming releases/events, including Hong Kong calendar dates and times with correct DST and midnight conversion; and (7) one cautious sentence interpreting the combined moves, explicitly separating inference from facts. Resolve yesterday from Asia/Hong_Kong and label the corresponding US/Eastern reporting date. Handle weekends and US holidays by identifying the latest completed session while keeping news dated correctly. Keep upcoming events separate from past events and exclude events already completed at retrieval. Use consistent instruments, observation cutoffs and prior-session comparisons; label proxies, delayed or unavailable data and fallback sources. Cite sources and show an as-of time in HKT. Use the skill's bundled render_snapshot.py and image-format.md workflow to render verified data programmatically into a clean portrait image with readable text, explicit signs and units, and clearly labelled proxies, missing data, sources and dates. Apply the approved dreamy visual system: soft blue/lavender gradients, mint and blush accents, lightly tinted rounded cards, dark navy text, a lavender interpretation panel, two prominent ETF cards, and three Treasury yield cards. Set footer notes in a distinct smaller monospaced font (19px at 1200px image width). Render ALL inline source markers—including those in bold metric labels, news cards and table cells—as small muted monospaced superscripts at about 60% of adjacent text size (14–19px), attached to the preceding word and never alone on a line. Use sentiment-labelled news cards: mint for supportive, rose for adverse, lavender for neutral/mixed. Base sentiment on verified market implications, not the sign of a statistic; matching consensus is ordinarily neutral. Present upcoming events in a table with HKT date/time | Event | What to watch, with one event per row even when times coincide; keep 'What to watch' factual and brief. Use the structured news, sectors and upcoming-event payload described in image-format.md; never reuse trial-specific data, dates or sentiment labels. Check full-size and 600px previews for clipped text, orphan citations, overlapping pills and crowded table cells. Include all sections in compact form: headline and interpretation above the figures, key market data in the middle, and the two most important past-event headlines plus the next-session HKT calendar below. Inspect the actual image for legibility, clipping and numerical accuracy before delivery. Save the final PNG through the available Library workflow and display it inline with a short accessible text fallback (normally 60–100 words) and real clickable source links/citations below. Do not duplicate the image with a 300+ word report. Never generate factual numbers or labels with a generative image model. If rendering, persistence or attachment is unavailable, explain the specific limitation and deliver verified compact text/tables for that run, aiming under 200 words plus sources; never claim a missing image was delivered or reuse a prior day's image. Avoid unsolicited trading recommendations.
